sit: Your teammate just picked up the puck along the boards. Three players from the other team are skating right toward them to try and steal it.
opts: Skate away from the pile into an empty patch of open ice and show your stick
Skate right up to your teammate to help them dig the puck out of the crowd
Stand completely still right where you are
Skate behind the other team's net to hide
explain: At this age, everyone loves to chase the puck like a swarm of bees! But if you jump into the pile, you bring another defender with you. Finding open ice makes you a great option and helps your teammate out.

sit: You just scooped up a loose puck! You look up and see two players from the other team standing straight ahead of you, but there is no one on the left side of the ice.
opts: Put your head down and try to skate right through the two defenders
Stop skating and wait for the defenders to take it
Steer your skates toward the empty left side and skate as fast as you can
Shoot the puck all the way down the ice from your own end
explain: We always want to carry the puck to the open ice! If you see a wall of players, don't try to crash through it. Use your edges, steer to the quiet ice, and use your speed.

sit: You are in the offensive zone trying to score, but a player on the other team steals the puck and starts skating fast toward your goalie.
opts: Chase the puck carrier directly from behind, trying to poke them with your stick
Stay by the other team's net and wait for your team to get the puck back
Skate to the bench because you are tired
Stop, turn around, and skate as hard as you can back toward your own net to help your goalie
explain: As soon as the other team gets the puck, it's time to play defense! Instead of just chasing the puck carrier, take the fastest path straight back to your net to protect the 'house' in front of your goalie.

sit: Your teammate is skating down the wing with the puck and is about to shoot on the goalie. You are skating right down the middle of the ice.
opts: Skate all the way into the corner to see if the puck misses the net
Stop at the side of the net with your stick flat on the ice, ready for a rebound
Skate up to your teammate and try to take the puck to shoot it yourself
Stop at the blue line and watch what happens
explain: Goalies make lots of saves, and the puck often bounces right back out! If you stop at the net with your stick on the ice, you'll be the first one there to tap in the loose change.

sit: A player digs the puck out of the corner right next to their own goalie. They decide to skate the puck directly across the front of their own net to get to the other side.
question: What is the player's mistake?
opts: They skated the puck through the danger zone in front of their own net instead of using the boards
They did not pass it backward off their own goalie's pads
They left the puck in the corner and skated away
They should have shot it at their own net to test their goalie
explain: The area right in front of your net is the danger zone! We never want to skate the puck across our own goalie's face because if we lose it, the other team gets an easy shot. Always use the boards to break out safely.

sit: You are stickhandling up the ice, but you accidentally lose the puck off the toe of your blade. It's sitting just a few feet away from you.
opts: Keep skating forward in a big wide circle to turn around and come back for it
Stop instantly, pivot, and jump right back on the puck before anyone else can get it
Give up and let the other team have it
Look at your stick to see if it's broken
explain: Mistakes happen to everyone! The best players are the ones who react the fastest when they lose the puck. Stopping on a dime instead of taking a big wide turn wins you the race back to the puck.

sit: When the puck is sliding slowly into the corner, you should stare right at the puck the entire time until it is safely on your stick.
tip: Take a picture before you touch the puck.
why: Taking a quick peek over your shoulder before you touch the puck helps you see where the bad guys are and where the open ice is so you can skate to safety right away.

sit: Your teammate intercepts a pass and has a clear breakaway! They are skating as fast as they can toward the other team's net.
opts: Celebrate by throwing your hands up at center ice because they are probably going to score
Go change on the bench
Skate backward slowly to watch
Skate hard right behind them to follow up on the play
explain: Even on a breakaway, the play isn't over until the puck is in the net. Following up hard means if the goalie makes a great save, you are right there to grab the rebound!

sit: A player on the other team has the puck directly behind your net. You are the only defender back.
opts: Stand right in front of your goalie, keeping your stick on the ice to protect the scoring area
Chase the player around the back of the net to try and steal the puck
Stand inside the net with your goalie
Skate up to the blue line and wait for them to come out
explain: They can't score from behind the net! If you chase them back there, you leave the front of the net wide open for a pass. Stay in the 'house' and make sure no one gets near your goalie.

sit: You are standing in the open ice. Your teammate has the puck and looks right at you. You want them to pass it.
opts: Wave your hands in the air and yell really loud so they see you
Hold your stick up in the air by your waist
Turn your back to them and start skating away
Tap your stick blade flat on the ice right where you want the puck to go
explain: A good pass needs a good target! Keeping your stick blade flat on the ice tells your teammate exactly where to send the puck, and it means you're ready to catch it immediately.

sit: You shoot the puck, and the goalie catches it in their glove. The referee blows the whistle loudly.
opts: Keep skating in and try to poke the puck out of the goalie's glove just in case
Stop immediately, turn away, and skate back toward your teammates
Shoot another puck at the net
Bump into the goalie
explain: When we hear the whistle, the play is completely dead. We always respect the goalie! Good hockey players stop on a dime and get ready for the next shift.

sit: You skate into the offensive zone and see that two of your teammates are already in the right corner trying to get the puck from a defender.
opts: Skate into the right corner to make it three teammates digging for the same puck
Skate back into your own defensive zone
Skate to the front of the net or the empty left side and get your stick ready
Stand right behind your two teammates in the corner
explain: If there are already two teammates on the puck, they don't need a third! By staying out of the corner and finding the quiet ice, you give them someone to pass to once they win the battle.

sit: The other team is attacking, but your goalie makes a huge save and passes the puck out to your defenseman.
opts: Turn up the ice, start skating forward, and look back for a pass
Keep standing in front of your goalie to protect them just in case
Skate backward up the ice
Skate into the corner and wait
explain: As soon as our team gets the puck, we want to go on offense! Start skating up the ice to stretch out the other team and give your defender a great option to move the puck forward.

sit: An attacker is skating fast right at you with the puck. You are the last defender back.
opts: Dive headfirst onto the ice to try and poke the puck away
Keep your body between the attacker and your net, steering them toward the boards
Step completely out of their way so they don't hit you
Skate straight at them as fast as you can and try to guess which way they will go
explain: If you dive or guess wrong, the attacker goes right past you for a breakaway. Keep your body between them and the net, and gently guide them to the outside boards where it's hard to score!

sit: When you are guarding a player without the puck in front of your net, you should hold your stick high in the air so you are ready to bat the puck if it flies up.
why: Most passes in hockey happen flat on the ice! Having an 'active stick' flat on the ice means you are always ready to intercept a pass before it reaches the dangerous player you are guarding.

sit: You get a great pass right in the middle of the ice. The only person between you and the goal is the goalie.
opts: Stop skating immediately to take a huge slapshot from really far away
Pass the puck backward to someone else
Skate the puck into the corner to be safe
Keep your feet moving, skate straight toward the net, and shoot
explain: When you have empty ice in front of you, take it! Moving your feet puts pressure on the goalie and gets you closer for a much better scoring chance.
